description:
We are CyberPookie, a team focused on building practical, data-driven solutions for real-world problems.

For the Field Shift challenge, we aim to use NASA Earth observation data, local soil information, and crop data to help farmers make better crop-rotation decisions and adapt to changing climate conditions.
summary:
TerraLoop is an intelligent agricultural decision-support platform designed to help smallholder farmers in Bangladesh build more resilient and sustainable farming strategies. By combining farm history, soil conditions, water availability, crop rotation optimization, and NASA Earth observation data, TerraLoop transforms traditional season-by-season farming into informed, multi-year agricultural planning.

The platform generates optimized 3–5 year crop rotation plans, evaluates soil health and nitrogen balance, tracks irrigation requirements, and simulates drought, flood, and extreme heat scenarios. Farmers can compare different strategies, explore adaptive alternatives, and understand how their decisions affect long-term productivity, profitability, and environmental sustainability.

Featuring interactive satellite mapping, visual farm simulations, NASA data integration, and personalized learning from previous harvests, TerraLoop provides a comprehensive view of a farm's past, present, and possible futures. Its Resilience Passport makes these insights portable through detailed reports and data exports.

Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 by Team CyberPookie, TerraLoop brings together Earth observation, agricultural modeling, and adaptive planning to help farmers make smarter decisions for a more resilient future.
details:
TerraLoop is an agricultural decision-support platform that helps smallholder farmers in Bangladesh plan smarter, more sustainable, and climate-resilient farming strategies. Instead of making decisions one season at a time, farmers can explore how different crop rotations will affect their land over the next 3–5 years.

What does it do and how does it work?

Farmers can select their farmland using interactive satellite maps, define field boundaries, specify soil conditions, irrigation limits, and record previous crop history. Using these inputs, TerraLoop's crop-rotation optimization engine evaluates eligible crops and generates multi-year planting strategies.

Its optimization engine uses a 64-candidate beam-search algorithm to evaluate crop sequences based on profitability, water requirements, soil health, crop diversity, nitrogen fixation, and biological compatibility. It also maintains seasonal water and nitrogen balances and models soil organic matter dynamics and erosion using the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE).

Farmers can simulate droughts, floods, and extreme heat events to see how their existing plans might perform under changing conditions. When a disruption occurs, TerraLoop can re-optimize the remaining seasons while preserving completed and unaffected seasons. Multiple strategies can also be compared side by side through interactive charts, agricultural metrics, and visual field simulations.

The platform incorporates NASA Earth observation resources, including NASA POWER, SRTM, and Worldview/GIBS, alongside modeled or derived indicators based on other NASA missions and datasets. Previous harvest outcomes can be recorded to calibrate future yield expectations for individual farms.

What benefits does it provide?

  • Better long-term planning: Helps farmers move beyond repetitive seasonal decisions through multi-year crop rotation strategies.
  • Water conservation: Accounts for irrigation requirements and annual water budgets to encourage more efficient water use.
  • Improved soil health: Considers nitrogen balance, legume rotation, residue management, organic matter, and erosion risks.
  • Climate resilience: Allows farmers to test different climate-disruption scenarios and explore alternative crop sequences.
  • Informed decision-making: Makes complex agricultural indicators understandable through visual simulations, comparisons, and explainable recommendations.
  • Continuous learning: Uses previous harvest observations to improve future farm-specific estimates.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to help smallholder farmers make better-informed decisions that protect their land while maintaining agricultural productivity and economic stability. By bringing together Earth observation data, agricultural modeling, and adaptive planning, TerraLoop aims to reduce the risks associated with monoculture, inefficient irrigation, declining soil fertility, and increasingly unpredictable climate conditions.

We designed the platform around Bangladesh's agricultural context, with regionally relevant crop profiles and demonstration farms from Rajshahi, Kurigram, and Rangpur. Ultimately, we envision a future where farmers can understand not only what to plant next season, but also how today's decisions will shape the productivity and resilience of their land years into the future.

What tools and technologies did we use?

TerraLoop was developed as a lightweight, browser-based application using:

  • Programming languages: JavaScript (modern ES Modules), HTML5, and CSS3.
  • Runtime: Node.js for the local development server.
  • Mapping: Leaflet.js, OpenStreetMap, Esri World Imagery, and NASA GIBS satellite imagery.
  • NASA resources: NASA POWER API, SRTM/NASADEM elevation data, Worldview/GIBS, and references to SMAP, GPM, ECOSTRESS, MODIS, Landsat, GRACE, FIRMS, and other Earth observation resources.
  • Visualization: HTML5 Canvas for procedural crop growth and environmental stress simulations, alongside interactive charts.
  • Agricultural modeling: Crop-rotation optimization, seasonal water and nitrogen balance, RUSLE soil erosion estimation, and soil organic matter dynamics.
  • Testing: Node.js native test runner with 48 automated tests.

The application uses vanilla JavaScript without React, Vue, external runtime dependencies, or a database server. Farm information is stored locally in the browser, allowing the planning and simulation engines to operate offline. NASA API connections and online map layers require an internet connection.

What makes TerraLoop creative and innovative?

Our central idea was to transform a farm into a kind of time machine. Rather than simply recommending a crop, TerraLoop allows farmers to explore the consequences of different decisions across several years.

One of its most distinctive features is its adaptive escape-route system. When a farmer introduces a drought, flood, or heat-wave scenario, the platform does not simply display a warning. It preserves the unaffected seasons and generates an alternative crop rotation for the remaining planning horizon.

We also developed a visual simulation studio where farmers can watch multiple crop-rotation strategies grow through six stages, from sowing to harvest. Environmental conditions visibly affect the fields, making the consequences of climate stress easier to understand.

Another innovative aspect is the integration of different agricultural factors into one planning system. Economic returns, irrigation limits, nitrogen fixation, pest and disease host breaks, residue practices, soil erosion, and crop diversity all influence the generated strategies. The Resilience Passport further provides transparent comparisons, model assumptions, and explainability information rather than presenting recommendations as unexplained results.

What factors did our team consider?

During development, we considered the practical realities of smallholder farming in Bangladesh:

  • Regional relevance: Crop choices, seasons, soil types, prices, and agricultural conditions were designed around Bangladesh's agro-climatic context.
  • Water availability: Irrigation limits and seasonal rainfall were considered to avoid generating unrealistic water-intensive rotations.
  • Soil sustainability: Nitrogen depletion, residue management, organic matter, and erosion were included in long-term planning.
  • Climate uncertainty: Drought, flooding, and extreme heat were treated as separate stress scenarios with crop-specific sensitivity.
  • Accessibility: The application was designed to run in a modern browser without installation, accounts, or complicated setup.
  • Transparency: We distinguish live NASA data connections from modeled indicators, reference benchmarks, and illustrative demonstration values.
  • Scientific limitations: We recognize that the current prototype is a decision-support model, not a validated crop-growth simulator or a replacement for local agronomic expertise.

TerraLoop is ultimately an attempt to make satellite data and agricultural science more accessible and actionable. By connecting the past, present, and future of a farm, we hope to help farmers make decisions that benefit both their harvests and the land they depend on.
